paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: seeing God's wonders is not the same as taking them to heart. Moses tells Israel they saw everything the LORD did in Egypt with their own eyes, "Yet to this day the LORD has not given you a mind to understand, eyes to see, or ears to hear." (Deut 29:2-4) I know that feeling, because I've watched the same cookie demo again and again and STILL burned the batch. Understanding is a gift, so we ask God for it, and we don't just stand there hoping we'll soak it up.

The covenant is for everybody, and that is good news. The leaders, the wood cutters, the water carriers and even those not there yet are all brought in, so that the LORD may "establish you today as His people." (Deut 29:11-15) But Moses also warns about a heart that hears the oath and says, "I will have peace, even though I walk in the stubbornness of my own heart." (Deut 29:19) That's a heart telling itself the batch is FINE while the timer is screaming. The call is to stay close to the LORD on purpose, because drifting to other gods leads to the ruin Moses describes, and Moses wants that for nobody.

Then he lands the plane: "The secret things belong to the LORD our God, but the things revealed belong to us and to our children forever, so that we may follow all the words of this law." (Deut 29:29) Some things God keeps to Himself, and that's okay, so we don't have to figure out everything. What He has shown us is ours, and it's given so we can DO it. So, baker, open the Word, follow what He's made plain, and trust Him with the rest. And stay close, because Moses is NOT done preaching yet.
